Let \(N=101\) and \(x=2^{-1}\). For a fixed denominator \(m\), write \(k=r+jm\) with \(1\le r\le m\), \(j\ge 0\). Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{N(r+jm)}{m}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \frac{Nr}{m}+jN\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \frac{Nr}{m}\right\rfloor+jN.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}x^{\lfloor Nk/m\rfloor}
=
\sum_{r=1}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}x^{\lfloor Nr/m\rfloor+jN}
=
\frac{\sum_{r=1}^{m}x^{\lfloor Nr/m\rfloor}}{1-x^N}.
\]

So the desired sum is

\[
S=\frac{1}{1-x^N}T,
\qquad
T=\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}\sum_{k=1}^{m}x^{\lfloor Nk/m\rfloor}.
\]

Now count the pairs \((m,k)\) giving each exponent \(q=\lfloor Nk/m\rfloor\). Let \(C_q\) be the number of pairs \(1\le k\le m\le N-1\) with \(\lfloor Nk/m\rfloor=q\).

For \(q=N\), we must have \(k=m\), so \(C_N=N-1\).

For \(q=N-1\), the condition is
\[
\frac{(N-1)m}{N}\le k<m,
\]
which has no integer solution, so \(C_{N-1}=0\).

For \(1\le q\le N-2\), the condition is
\[
\frac{qm}{N}\le k<\frac{(q+1)m}{N}.
\]
Since \(N=101\) is prime and \(1\le q,q+1\le N-1\), the endpoints are not integers, and the interval has length \(<1\). Hence the number of integer \(k\) for a given \(m\) is

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{(q+1)m}{N}\right\rfloor-
\left\lfloor \frac{qm}{N}\right\rfloor.
\]

Using
\[
\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}\left\lfloor \frac{am}{N}\right\rfloor
=
\frac{(a-1)(N-1)}2
\qquad (1\le a\le N-1),
\]
we get

\[
C_q=
\sum_{m=1}^{N-1}
\left(
\left\lfloor \frac{(q+1)m}{N}\right\rfloor-
\left\lfloor \frac{qm}{N}\right\rfloor
\right)
=
\frac{N-1}{2}.
\]

For \(N=101\), this means

\[
C_q=50\quad(1\le q\le 99),\qquad C_{100}=0,\qquad C_{101}=100.
\]

Therefore

\[
T=50\sum_{q=1}^{99}2^{-q}+100\cdot 2^{-101}.
\]

Since \(\sum_{q=1}^{99}2^{-q}=1-2^{-99}\),

\[
T=50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}
=50-100\cdot 2^{-101}.
\]

Thus

\[
S=\frac{50-100\cdot 2^{-101}}{1-2^{-101}}
=\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}
=50-\frac{50}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{50-\frac{50}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
